introduction_markdown:
**General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Geography (0750), Paper 3, ADVANCED LEVEL, June 2022. Duration: three and a quarter hours.**

Answer FOUR questions in all. Answer question ONE and three others, choosing at least ONE question from SECTION B and TWO from SECTION C. Question ONE carries thirty-one marks and the rest carry twenty-three marks each.

Only the required number of questions will be marked.

In answering questions on this paper, you are encouraged to refer to your own field and practical work where relevant. Credit will be awarded for such references.

Candidates are advised NOT to attempt the questions on field investigations if such an exercise has not been carried out.

Marks will be awarded for well annotated maps and diagrams where these are relevant.

You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers.

Calculators are allowed.

Materials required: Topographic map, graph paper and two outline maps of Cameroon.

questions.enonce_markdown:
a) Calculate the interquartile range and state its significance. The formula for calculating the interquartile range is stated as:

IQR = Q3 - Q1

Where IQR is the interquartile range, Q3 is the upper quartile and Q1 is the lower quartile. (5 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Step 1 - rank the data (1 mark).** 2,275; 3,500; 5,500; 8,750; 10,000; 16,800; 18,000; 20,750; 28,200; 29,250 (n = 10).

**Step 2 - median.** (10,000 + 16,800) / 2 = 13,400.

**Step 3 - quartiles (2 marks).** Split the ranked data into a lower half (2,275; 3,500; 5,500; 8,750; 10,000) and an upper half (16,800; 18,000; 20,750; 28,200; 29,250).

- Lower quartile Q1 = the median of the lower half = 5,500.
- Upper quartile Q3 = the median of the upper half = 20,750.

**Step 4 - interquartile range (1 mark).** IQR = Q3 - Q1 = 20,750 - 5,500 = **15,250 people**.

(Another accepted method uses the positions (n + 1)/4 and 3(n + 1)/4, that is 2.75th and 8.25th values: Q1 = 5,000 and Q3 = 22,612.5, so IQR = 17,612.5; the candidate who shows a clear method receives the marks.)

**Significance (1 mark).** The interquartile range measures the spread (dispersion) of the middle 50 per cent of the villages and is not affected by extreme values. Here it is larger than the median (13,400), so the village sizes are very different from one another: the population is unevenly distributed in the Sub Division, with a few large villages (F, J, B) and several very small ones (C, H, E). A small IQR would have shown that most villages were similar in size.

*Marks: ranking 1; Q1 and Q3 2; IQR 1; significance 1.*

b) Using the outline map of the area attached below, represent the data by means of choropleth map. Use a scale of 1:2000 and divide the population into 5 classes or groups. (8 marks)

![fig-1](gce-al-geography-2022-p3-officiel-cameroun_exercice_3_fig_1.png)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Method (a choropleth map shades areas according to class values, from light to dark).**

1. **Class interval (2 marks).** Range = 29,250 - 2,275 = 26,975. Divided by 5 classes this gives about 5,395, rounded to a convenient equal interval of **6,000**.

| Class | Population | Villages | Shading |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 2,000 - 7,999 | C, H, E | lightest |
| 2 | 8,000 - 13,999 | G, A | light |
| 3 | 14,000 - 19,999 | I, D | medium |
| 4 | 20,000 - 25,999 | B | dark |
| 5 | 26,000 - 31,999 | J, F | darkest |

2. **Shading (3 marks).** Use one colour (or one pattern of dots or lines) with an increasing density from the lowest to the highest class, so that the eye reads a clear gradation. Shade each zone completely and neatly; the letters A to J remain visible.
3. **Key and title (2 marks).** Fill in the key with the five classes and their shading, in order; give the map a title (for example "Population of ten villages in a Sub Division") and write the scale (1:2000, as demanded in the question) under it.
4. **Presentation (1 mark).** Clean, neat work inside the frame.

![fig-2](gce-al-geography-2022-p3-officiel-cameroun_exercice_3_fig_2.png)

*Remark for credit: because the areas of the villages are not given, the map shows total population and not density; a choropleth map is better drawn with densities, so the candidate may mention this limitation.*

questions.enonce_markdown:
c) Describe any TWO problems associated with each of the following areas:

i) areas of high population concentration

ii) areas of low population concentration. (6 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(c)(i) Areas of high population concentration (villages F, J and B; in Cameroon, for example, large cities such as Douala and Yaoundé or the densely settled Western Highlands) - 3 marks, any two problems.**

- **Pressure on land and housing**: overcrowding, shortage of land, slums and land disputes, and fragmentation of farms in rural areas.
- **Pressure on social services and utilities**: schools, hospitals, water, electricity and transport are overstretched.
- **Unemployment and underemployment**, and the growth of the informal sector, because the jobs do not keep pace with the population.
- **Environmental problems**: pollution, refuse and waste water, deforestation and soil exhaustion, flooding and erosion on cleared slopes.
- **Insecurity and the spread of diseases**, and traffic congestion in towns.

**(c)(ii) Areas of low population concentration (villages C, H and E; for example the forest of the East and South Regions or the dry parts of the Far North) - 3 marks, any two problems.**

- **Lack of labour** and of a market: little agricultural production and no economies of scale, so industry and trade develop poorly.
- **Poor social amenities and infrastructure**: schools, health centres, roads and electricity are costly to provide to few people and are therefore lacking (the threshold population is not reached).
- **Isolation and rural exodus**: young people leave for the towns, leaving an ageing population.
- **Under-use of resources**: good land, forests or minerals remain undeveloped.
- **Low tax revenue and weak political representation**, so little public investment.

*Marks: each problem described (not just named) 1 to 1.5.*

questions.enonce_markdown: d) What TWO measures can be adopted to solve the problems associated with each of the areas cited in c i) and ii) above? (4 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(d)(i) For the areas of high concentration (2 marks, any two).**

- **Decentralisation and a balanced regional development**: create jobs, industries, universities and services in other regions, so as to reduce the pull of the big cities.
- **Planning and housing**: town planning, new housing estates and satellite towns, upgrading of slums, and better water, electricity and transport networks.
- **Family planning and education** to reduce the rate of population growth, and intensive agriculture (fertilisers, improved seeds) to feed more people from less land.

**(d)(ii) For the areas of low concentration (2 marks, any two).**

- **Provide infrastructure and services**: roads, electricity, water, schools and health centres, so that people are willing to stay or to settle.
- **Economic incentives**: credit and subsidies for farmers, agricultural and agro-industrial projects, processing industries and markets in the rural areas, and tax relief for investors.
- **Resettlement and planned settlement schemes** to move people from overcrowded areas to the empty ones (with security of land tenure).

*Marks: 1 per measure (two for (i) and two for (ii)).*
